beats.why_this_beat: This is the visual keynote — the full ensemble's first appearance, establishing the fire-town square, the unlit staff, and each character's signature posture and position.

annotations: I'm here! I'm the MOST ready!
beats.why_this_beat: Mango's entrance establishes her as the eager foil — all speed and confidence, arriving before anyone else, her physicality contrasting with the patience April will demand.

annotations: I'll watch. I'll be still. I'll be near.
beats.why_this_beat: Fern's entrance beat establishes her as the observer-counterpoint to Mango's energy — stillness as its own kind of readiness, the spotter's instinct before it has a name.

annotations: And how HOT? And how HIGH?
beats.why_this_beat: Riddle's entrance from above — elevated, questioning, angular — establishes her as the intellect of the group, the one who needs to understand before she can act.

annotations: You learn both together or don't learn at all
three dark little heads at the edge of the night
beats.why_this_beat: The central teaching moment — April delivers the chapter's thesis ('the fire AND the frame') and the ensemble is arranged in the call-and-response formation that will define the entire book.

annotations: We will learn them! We'll SOAR!
They heard the word FIRE. The FRAME blew away.
beats.why_this_beat: The chorus responds with pure enthusiasm but unconsciously emphasizes FIRE over FRAME — this is the chapter's subtle dramatic irony, the seed of every mistake to come.

annotations: The safety circle — you step IN to begin
draw it with chalk, draw it with feet
beats.why_this_beat: The first concrete step of the ritual is physically demonstrated — April on her knees drawing the boundary that will protect them, grounding the abstract 'frame' in a real chalk line.

The ensemble physically commits to the circle — each friend's entrance style (leap, walk, swoop, drop) reflects their character, and the act of stepping in transforms them from audience to participants.
The scorch mark gets its first close-up as April introduces the spotter role — her fingers on the old burn connect the abstract lesson to a personal cost the reader doesn't yet understand.

annotations: three little dragons asleep in the air
Tomorrow we learn what the wet towel knows
just starting to wake from its sleep
beats.why_this_beat: The closing image — the unlit wicks blazing with borrowed sunset light, the five friends held inside the circle, the promise of 'tomorrow' — leaves the reader wanting to know what comes next.
